It doesn't have to be display: block.

As a consequence of `content-visibility: hidden` use, the `hidden=until-found` value only has an effect on elements that are also affected by `content-visibility: hidden`. Specifically, through another layer of indirection, it only affects elements that can be affected by layout containment (or paint or size containment -- the criteria are the same). These are listed (or rather its negation is listed) in [css-contain-2](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-contain-2/#containment-layout):

> If the element does not generate a principal box (as is the case with display values of contents or none), or its principal box is an internal table box other than table-cell, or an internal ruby box, or a non-atomic inline-level box, layout containment has no effect.

So, as an example `display: contents` or `display: none` would not be affected by `hidden=until-found` in a way that a `display: block` or `display: flex` would be, assuming no other criteria prevents the containment from applying.

Instead of saying `must` here, I think we should simply say that elements that cannot be affected by layout containment are also unaffected by `hidden=until-found`. This is a different behavior from behaviors that any other truthy value* of `hidden` attribute imposes, since other values are implemented as `display: none` which can affect all elements.
